content: 1. A study conducted as part of the CHAPAS-4 trial evaluated the pharmacokinetics, safety, and antiviral efficacy of tenofovir alafenamide in children and adolescents with chronic hepatitis B. This randomized, double-blind study provided critical insights into the drug's performance in this population. 2. Research by Schwarz et al. demonstrated no detectable resistance to tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) treatment in children and adolescents with chronic hepatitis B after 24 weeks of therapy, highlighting the drug's effectiveness and resistance profile. 3. The aspartate transaminase-to-platelet ratio index (APRI) has been shown to be a valuable tool in assessing hepatic fibrosis and liver inflammation in adolescents with HBeAg-positive chronic hepatitis B, as reported by Zhijian et al. 4. Transient elastography, combined with multi-parameter models, has been validated as an effective method for assessing liver fibrosis in young children with chronic hepatitis B virus infection, as demonstrated in studies by Luo et al. and Xu et al. 5. The PEG-B-ACTIVE liver elasticity substudy highlighted the utility of transient elastography in evaluating liver fibrosis in children with chronic hepatitis B, providing a non-invasive alternative to traditional biopsy methods. 6. Zhang et al. developed a simple, non-invasive model to predict significant fibrosis in children with chronic hepatitis B, offering a practical approach for clinical settings. 7. Hepatic histology studies in treatment-naïve children with chronic hepatitis B in the United States and Canada revealed a high prevalence of untreated chronic hepatitis, emphasizing the need for improved management strategies, as reported by Rodriguez-Baez et al. 8. Yang et al. found that hepatocellular carcinoma occurs at a younger age in African populations, particularly in association with chronic hepatitis B, underscoring the importance of early detection and intervention. 9. Mason et al. explored HBV DNA integration and clonal hepatocyte expansion in patients with chronic hepatitis B considered immune-tolerant, providing insights into the disease's pathogenesis. 10. A five-year randomized study by Fung et al. compared tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) with emtricitabine/TDF in lamivudine-resistant hepatitis B, demonstrating the long-term efficacy of these regimens. 11. Surial et al. reported significant weight and metabolic changes in people living with HIV after switching from TDF to tenofovir alafenamide (TAF), highlighting the metabolic implications of antiretroviral therapy. 12. The CHAPAS-4 trial supported the use of improved second-line treatment options for children with HIV, as summarized by Cayden P. 13. Ling et al. emphasized the high prevalence of untreated chronic hepatitis B among children in North America, calling for better screening and treatment protocols. 14. Lok et al. provided standardized nomenclature and management recommendations for antiviral drug-resistant HBV, facilitating consistent clinical practices. 15. Locarnini reviewed the pathways of primary resistance, multidrug resistance, and cross-resistance in HBV, emphasizing the challenges of treatment failure. 16. Studies by Fung et al. and Yim et al. documented the evolution of multidrug-resistant hepatitis B virus during sequential therapy, highlighting the need for robust antiviral strategies. 17. Pallier et al. described the dynamics of lamivudine resistance in hepatitis B virus, providing insights into the emergence of resistant mutants during prolonged therapy. 18. Leung reviewed recent data on the treatment of chronic hepatitis B with nucleos(t)ide analogues, summarizing their efficacy and limitations. 19. Yeh et al. reported the clearance of original YIDD-motif mutants in HBV with the emergence of distinct lamivudine-resistant mutants during extended therapy. 20. Mokaya et al. presented evidence of tenofovir resistance in chronic HBV infection among South African adults, raising concerns about the long-term efficacy of this treatment. 21. The EASL 2017 guidelines provided comprehensive recommendations for managing hepatitis B virus infection, emphasizing evidence-based approaches. 22. Huang et al. compared the efficacy of lamivudine plus adefovir versus entecavir in treating lamivudine-resistant chronic hepatitis B, concluding that entecavir offers superior outcomes. 23. Lim et al. conducted a randomized trial of entecavir plus adefovir in patients with lamivudine-resistant chronic hepatitis B, demonstrating improved virologic responses. 24. Sherman et al. reported improved virologic, biochemical, and serologic outcomes with entecavir therapy in lamivudine-refractory chronic hepatitis B over 96 weeks. 25. Hyun et al. compared the efficacy of lamivudine versus entecavir in patients with HBV-related decompensated cirrhosis, finding entecavir to be more effective. 26. Yim et al. evaluated the addition of adefovir versus switching to entecavir in lamivudine-resistant chronic hepatitis B, providing long-term data from a multicenter cohort study. 27. Byun et al. conducted a randomized trial of tenofovir alafenamide for drug-resistant hepatitis B, demonstrating its efficacy in patients switching from TDF. 28. Yamashige et al. reported the effectiveness of tenofovir alafenamide in chronic hepatitis B patients with poor responses to previous nucleos(t)ide analogues. 29. Yang et al. conducted a systematic review and network meta-analysis on the efficacy and cost-effectiveness of antiviral regimens for entecavir-resistant hepatitis B. 30. Liang et al. questioned whether monotherapy with TDF is sufficient for patients with multiple nucleos(t)ide analogue treatment failures in hepatitis B. 31. Yim et al. presented long-term data on tenofovir-based combination therapy or monotherapy for multidrug-resistant chronic hepatitis B, emphasizing its clinical utility. 32. Chen et al. identified the HBV mutation pattern rtA181S + T184I + M204I as a contributor to multidrug resistance, based on a large cohort of Chinese patients. 33. Wandera et al. reviewed the genetic multiplicity of HBV and associated lamivudine resistance mutations in HBV/HIV co-infection in western Kenya. 34. LG et al. demonstrated that alanine aminotransferase is an inadequate surrogate marker for detecting lamivudine resistance in hepatitis B. 35. The AASLD 2016 guidelines outlined evidence-based recommendations for treating chronic hepatitis B, emphasizing individualized care. 36. WHO guidelines provided comprehensive strategies for preventing, diagnosing, and managing chronic hepatitis B, including mother-to-child transmission prevention. 37. Boek et al. evaluated the implementation of near point-of-care viral load testing in public health facilities across sub-Saharan Africa, demonstrating its feasibility and impact. 38. Luo et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the clinical effect of point-of-care HIV diagnosis in infants, highlighting its potential to improve outcomes. 39. Trickey et al. compared hepatitis C virus point-of-care RNA viral load testing with laboratory-based testing, demonstrating improved uptake and reduced turnaround times. 40. The WHO Expert Committee on Specifications for Pharmaceutical Preparations provided updated recommendations for diagnostics and treatment delivery systems. 41. Hughes et al. reviewed the epidemiology, pathogenesis, and management of hepatitis delta virus, emphasizing the challenges in addressing this co-infection. 42. Stockdale et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the global prevalence of hepatitis delta virus infection, providing critical epidemiological insights. 43. Fattovich et al. reported the influence of hepatitis delta virus infection on morbidity and mortality in compensated cirrhosis type B, based on the Eurohep study. 44. Kamal et al. highlighted the impact of viremia on liver-related outcomes in patients with hepatitis delta virus infection, based on long-term data from secondary care centers. 45. The EASL 2023 guidelines provided updated recommendations for managing hepatitis delta virus, emphasizing evidence-based approaches. 46. Palom et al. reported long-term clinical outcomes in patients with chronic hepatitis delta, emphasizing the importance of persistent viremia and genotype in treatment response.
